To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Spitzer IRS spectroscopic data show the first detection of [Ne II], and [Fe I], as well as upper limits on [S I] toward T Tauri disks.

we detect [Ne II] in 20% of T Tauri disks, [Fe I] in 9% of T Taurus disks, and H_2 S(1) in one Taurus disk; that the [Ne II] emission is consistent with X-ray irradiated disks, the [Fe I] emission indicates the presence of gas disks with M_gas > 0.1M_J, and the H_2 emission is higher than expected from current disk models.
we have detected [Ne II] emission in ~20% of the sources, and we find [Ne II] fluxes consistent with X-ray irradiated gas in the inner disk around stars with L_X = 1030-31 erg s^(- 1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of disk physics, including the gas mass and temperature structure, and the heating mechanisms of disk atmospheres.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current models of disk chemistry and excitation, including X-rays, UV, and shocks, are not able to explain all the observed line fluxes and flux ratios, and thus more work is required to understand the physical and chemical processes in T Tauri disks.
the current models of gas heating in disks are not yet complete, and that additional processes are required to explain the observations.

the observed [Ne II], H_2, and [Fe I], lines are consistent with the presence in the disk of hot and warm gas in a range of densities and excitation temperatures, but the observed [Ne I] and H_2 3-0 and 2-1 S(1) lines are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the [Fe I] line is a good tracer of gas-rich disks, while the [Ne II] lines can be used as a diagnostic for X-ray emission from the central star.
the observed [Ne II], H_2 2-1 S(1) and [Fe I], 1-0 lines are consistent with the presence and excitation of warm (~100 K) gas-phase disks around T Tauris stars.
the gas mass in the inner disk is ~10-100 times higher than predicted by current models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the [Ne II] lines provide a new and useful diagnostic to probe the X-ray-irradiated disk gas in T Tauri systems.
gas-phase emission is a ubiquitous phenomenon toward T Tauri disks and that it can be used to constrain disk models.
gas-phase lines are a powerful tool for constraining the gas mass and temperature structure in circumstellar disks.
